title: Conjugation identifies the tensor pullback square comparison
statement: Let $f:X\to S$, $f':X'\to T$, $g:T\to S$ and $v:X'\to X$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme], with $f\circ v=g\circ f'$ (written $v \gg f=f' \gg g$ in Lean). Let $A$ be an arbitrary module on $S$. Write $P_k$ for tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback], $R_k$ for pushforward, and use the pinned adjunctions [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction]. The inverse conjugate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] of the pushforward square $R_v R_f\to R_{vf}\to R_{f'g}\to R_{f'}R_g$, evaluated at $A$, equals the composite $P_{f'}P_g A\to P_{f'g}A\to P_{vf}A\to P_vP_f A$ constructed using the tensor composition isomorphisms [lem-sc-picard-canonical-base-change-comparisons] and the equality of the composite morphisms. This asserts coherence of the composition comparisons; it involves neither a base-change morphism nor a counit formula. The exact equality is lean.statement.

source.place: Composition of pullback and pushforward; with the adjunction in 0096 and the square mate in 08HY.

proof.text: Use the definition of picardTensorComparison as leftAdjointUniq for the pinned tensor adjunction and ordinary pullback adjunction. Unfold conjugateIsoEquiv to prove that the comparison and its inverse both have identity conjugates. Bundle the four composition factors in a natural isomorphism tensorComp; its component is definitionally picardTensorCompIso.

Expand tensorComp.inv. Apply conjugateEquiv_comp three times with the ordinary composite adjunction and the two mixed composite adjunctions. The two whiskering laws identify the whiskered inverse comparisons with whiskered identities. conjugateEquiv_pullbackComp_inv identifies the ordinary composition factor with pushforwardComp.hom. Cancel identities. Apply the inverse equivalence to obtain the inverse mate equation; equality of conjugate isomorphisms and their inverse morphisms gives the forward mate equation.

For equal scheme morphisms k and l, substitute l = k. The pushforward equality comparison is the identity, checked on every module and open using pushforwardCongr_hom_app_app. Its inverse conjugate is the identity by conjugateEquiv_symm_id. This gives eqToHom of the tensor functor equality. Separately substitute the equality to identify the component of this functor equality transport with the hom of the object equality isomorphism.

Apply conjugateEquiv_symm_comp twice to the three-factor pushforward square. Substitute the forward composition mate, equality mate, and inverse composition mate. Evaluate the resulting natural transformation at A. Use the equality-transport component identity and the tensorComp component identity, then the hom formulas for composite and inverse isomorphisms and associativity, to obtain exactly the displayed equality. No assumption that the square is cartesian is used.

proof_origin.place: Adjunction uniqueness and composition, made into Lean using Mathlib conjugation composition and whiskering laws; equality transport by substitution and evaluation of the bundled tensor composition isomorphism.

lean.statement:
theorem picardTensorSquareConjugacy
    {X S T X' : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (f' : X' ⟶ T)
    (g : T ⟶ S) (v : X' ⟶ X) (e : v ≫ f = f' ≫ g) (A : S.Modules) :
    let adj : ∀ {Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (k : Y ⟶ Z), tensorPullback k ⊣ pushforward k :=
      fun k ↦ Classical.choose (exists_tensorPullbackAdjunction k)
    ((conjugateEquiv ((adj f).comp (adj v)) ((adj g).comp (adj f'))).symm
      ((pushforwardComp v f).hom ≫ (pushforwardCongr e).hom ≫
        (pushforwardComp f' g).inv)).app A =
    (picardTensorCompIso f' g A ≪≫
      eqToIso (congrArg (fun k ↦ (tensorPullback k).obj A) e.symm) ≪≫
      (picardTensorCompIso v f A).symm).hom
